doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Ballyhooing through town and the show schedule
summary: Reel 2 begins with the platform and banner, street-corner ballyhoo, and the 8 to 9:30 show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So anyway, that was a part of the show. I used to like to see him do those things. He'd get on those rings and things like that, and he had some bars.
Was it all on this platform? All on this platform. It was a big platform.
Well, the platform was fully as big as this room.

Yeah, and then you'd have all these things assembled on this platform. That's right. That's right. And you had set up the instrument. That's right. And then, so start. Now what happened? How'd you get the people in there? What'd you do?
We would ballyhoo through town. When we got to town, Doc would have a banner.

The top part was Doc Moon's medicine show, famous entertainers and different things like that. And showing at 346 Mott Street or some street like that, that's starting at 8 o'clock. Well, people was used to that kind of stuff in those days, and they would wait for it. You know, they never heard anything. You know, they didn't get too much entertainment. No radio or television in those days.
But we would play on the street corners, something similar to the way the bands used to ballyhoo and Baton Rouge advertising their dances.

Uh-huh. And people used to just lay for those medicine shows, because that was a regular occurrence. And when, when, when that, oh, about 6 o'clock people would start congregating around that platform, waiting for the show. See? When did the show start?
About 8 o'clock. It would last from about 8 to 9.30. Uh-huh. Hour and a half show usually.
